documents.abstract: The Generative AI (GAI) is reshaping the temporal and spatial organization of college learning and the perceived boundary crossing between teacher-assigned tasks and self-directed learning. This study developed and validated a scale to assess college students’ attention boundary management in GAI-mediated learning. Analyzing data from 1904 students at 3 colleges in China, the study established a five-dimensional structure: Flexibility, Fragmentation, Immersion, Positive Spillover, and Negative Spillover. Exploratory and Confirmatory Factor Analysis confirmed the scale’s psychometric properties. A Latent Profile Analysis identified four distinct student profiles, Protective, Strained, Overextended, and Engaged Permeability Management. Supplementary heterogeneity analyses examined differences across the four profiles by gender, grade level, university, purposes and duration of AI use, and other learning-related characteristics. Based on these, this study proposed profile-specific recommendations. The study provides a validated instrument for assessing students’ attention boundaries in GAI-mediated learning, identifies heterogeneous student profiles, and offers differentiated practical implications.

Money Tree is an ongoing, AI-assisted experimental research program investigating whether reproducible forward-looking information can be detected in chronological systems that are nominally or apparently random. Mega Millions is used as a deliberately difficult experimental target because its outcomes are discrete, chronological, publicly observable, externally generated, and designed to be unpredictable. The objective is not simply to predict lottery numbers. The lottery serves as a stress test for a broader question: can weak forward-looking structure be distinguished from coincidence, false discovery, data leakage, adaptive overfitting, or artifacts created by the way data are represented? The project began in 2026 with a simple historical-frequency question and evolved into a software research laboratory incorporating walk-forward evaluation, matched random controls, Monte Carlo testing, independent analytical engines, falsification procedures, a centralized Referee layer, AI specialist reviews, and prospective high-volume experimentation. This research is being released while it is still in progress. No claim of reliable lottery prediction is made. Positive, negative, inconclusive, and failed experiments are intentionally preserved in the research record. Collaboration is a primary purpose of this release. We welcome researchers, independent investigators, mathematicians, statisticians, software developers, and others working with stochastic processes, sequential prediction, complex systems, information theory, experimental mathematics, random-number testing, anomaly detection, or other noisy chronological systems. We are particularly interested in people who have methods, datasets, criticisms, or ongoing experiments that could independently challenge this framework. We are also interested in helping evaluate outside experiments or datasets where our developing zero-trust, walk-forward, matched-control methodology may be useful. A rigorous demonstration that one of our ideas is wrong is considered a successful contribution. The project was initiated and directed by Troy Stuart, who began without a computer-programming or computer-science background and learned AI prompting, Python development workflows, Visual Studio Code, GitHub, version control, testing, and experimental research practices while building the project step by step. ChatGPT, known throughout the project as “Chappie,” has served as a substantive AI research collaborator in research framing, discussion, drafting, code-oriented guidance, critique, documentation, and coordination of independent AI specialist reviews. Troy Stuart remains the human project originator, decision-maker, and accountable author. Research status: Ongoing.Version: 1.0Release date: October 2, 2026.

Designing effective heuristics for diverse combinatorial optimization problems requires substantial expertise and repeated search. Large language models (LLMs) automate heuristic generation and refinement, but heuristic search typically depends on evaluation feedback from the problem being optimized. Generalizing to new problem definitions using only source-task feedback therefore remains a central challenge. We introduce MECo, an LLM-driven multi-task evolutionary framework for zero-shot cross-problem generalization. MECo maintains task-conditioned heuristic populations and uses a transfer gap based on cross-task population performance to guide their interactions. These interactions enable the transfer and recombination of heuristics. A complementary selection criterion then constructs a compact heuristic set by rewarding each member's additional coverage of source combinations. The selected set is applied to target problems without further search or adaptation. Experiments on 32 problem variants across vehicle routing (VRP) and flexible job-shop scheduling (FJSP) show that MECo achieves the lowest mean costs compared with eight automated heuristic design (AHD) baselines under the same budgets. On out-of-domain problems, it outperforms the strongest baseline in each family. Moreover, integrating the framework of MECo with different AHD methods improves their ID and OOD performance in both families, supporting its effectiveness across different methods.

ABSTRACT Background Manual prescription of liver MRI volumes introduces inter‐operator variability and prolongs exam duration. Artificial intelligence (AI)‐based prescription has been demonstrated, but existing work has been limited to single‐vendor settings. Purpose To develop and validate an AI model for automated liver MRI prescription using a large, consecutive, multicenter dataset encompassing multiple vendors, field strengths, localizer sequences, and liver pathologies. Study Type Retrospective. Population A total of 11,012 patients (5928 female) who underwent liver MRI exams across three vendors (GE HealthCare, Philips Healthcare, Siemens Healthineers) at three institutions, split into training/validation/test sets (70/10/20%). Liver disorders included cirrhosis, ascites, portal hypertension, and iron overload. Field Strength/Sequence Three‐plane localizers acquired using single‐shot fast spin echo (68.3%) and gradient echo (31.7%) at 1.5 T (52.8%) and 3 T (47.2%). Assessment A YOLOv8 object detection model was trained to detect the liver, torso, and arms on localizer images. Automated prescription accuracy was assessed using three‐dimensional intersection‐over‐union (IoU 3D ) for axial, coronal, and sagittal prescriptions. Subgroup analyses evaluated performance across technical and patient‐related factors. Statistical Tests Mann–Whitney U tests with Bonferroni correction, Kruskal‐Wallis tests, Wilcoxon signed‐rank tests, Spearman correlation. Effect sizes were calculated using rank‐biserial correlation ( r rb ) and epsilon‐squared ( ε 2 ). p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results Median axial prescription IoU 3D was 0.963 (interquartile range: 0.946–0.976), with median IoU 3D above 0.940 for coronal and sagittal prescriptions. For axial prescriptions, margins less than 4 mm in each direction were required to achieve complete coverage of manual prescriptions in 90% of cases in the held‐out test set. Effects were negligible to small across vendors, field strengths, localizer sequences, and patient factors ( r rb ≤ 0.16, ε 2 ≤ 0.01). Data Conclusion A single multivendor model achieved accurate automated liver MRI prescription without clinically meaningful performance differences across vendors, field strengths, localizer sequences, or patient factors. Evidence Level 2. Technical Efficacy Stage 1.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) represent a major occupational health concern among informal workers, particularly traditional Nypa palm handicraft workers who are frequently exposed to repetitive movements and prolonged non-ergonomic working postures. This study aimed to investigate the association between ergonomic and workplace environmental factors and MSDs severity levels among Nypa handicraft workers in traditional home-based industries. An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 150 Nypa handicraft workers in Palembang, South Sumatra, Indonesia. MSDs severity was assessed using the Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ)/Nordic Body Map (NBM), while work-related factors included working posture, repetitive hand movements, daily working hours, employment duration, and workload. Workplace environmental conditions, including temperature, relative humidity, and illumination, were measured using a thermohygrometer and lux meter. Data were analyzed using chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression.The results showed that 65.3% of workers experienced mild MSDs and 34.7% experienced moderate MSDs, with the lower back, shoulders, neck, and wrists being the most frequently affected body regions. Bivariate analysis indicated that high-risk working posture was significantly associated with higher MSDs severity levels (OR=2.642; 95% CI: 1.260–5.539; p=0.009). Furthermore, abnormal BMI was associated with MSDs severity levels (p=0.016). The findings indicate that non-ergonomic working posture was an important occupational factor associated with MSDs severity among traditional Nypa handicraft workers. Ergonomic interventions, including improved working posture, workstation redesign, adequate rest periods, and workplace environmental management, are recommended to reduce MSDs risk and promote safer working conditions in traditional home-based industries.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: We present Muslim, a production Arabic voice AI platform serving grounded, sourced Islamic knowledge to real users. Beyond a real-time voice pipeline (NeMo Arabic ASR, an OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint, self-hosted TTS) and a deterministic multi-source retrieval layer routed across six Model Context Protocol servers, we report three things a research prototype typically lacks. First, a released family of fine-tuned Arabic Islamic model artifacts: an efficient tool-routing LLM (Muslim-6B-PRO, 5.94B parameters) and a Modern Standard Arabic TTS model (Fasih-TTS-V1) that ranks 5th of 17 overall and 2nd of 11 open-weight systems on the community-voted Arabic TTS Arena for MSA. Second, an account and metering layer - a free per-account turn allowance, capacity-aware refusal, and email verification deferred to the point it actually matters - that turns an open demo into an operable, abuse-resistant product. Third, a three-layer observability stack (liveness, error reporting, product analytics) built specifically around the system's characteristic failure mode: a GPU-bound agent host going silent while the web tier keeps serving normally. We report real, measured latency and accuracy figures (98.4% recitation-validation accuracy on 124 cases; end-to-end voice latency of 0.9-1.7s) and discuss the concrete engineering trade-offs and limitations of running an Islamic-knowledge voice product in production.

This review evaluates the performance of natural-zeolite concrete under acidic and sulfate attack. The review discusses the literature on visual deterioration, weight loss, erosion depth, compressive strength retention, service life, and microstructural characteristics. The findings indicate that the durability performance of natural-zeolite concrete depends on the type of aggressive environment and the zeolite replacement level. Under sulfate exposure, natural zeolite improves durability by consuming calcium hydroxide and promoting the formation of additional calcium silicate hydrate (C-S-H) . It also reduces gypsum and ettringite formation, which improves compressive strength retention and extends the service life of concrete. One study showed that 20% zeolite extended service life from 15 to 35 months and maintained more than 75% relative compressive strength after 1050 days of sodium sulfate exposure. The results are study-specific and should not be considered a universal optimum. In contrast, the reported performance under sulfuric acid attack remains inconsistent. However, higher replacement levels (15%–30%) have also been associated with increased surface deterioration and strength loss under severe acid exposure. The review demonstrates that sulfuric acid is more aggressive than hydrochloric acid. However, differences in acid concentration, pH, exposure duration, and solution renewal limit direct comparison. The review also highlights that combining zeolite with tuff can partially mitigate tuff's adverse effects under acidic conditions. In addition, recent advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning demonstrate considerable potential for predicting and optimizing the performance of zeolite concrete by capturing nonlinear relationships. However, applying AI-based approaches to predict sulfuric-acid-induced deterioration and the sulfate resistance of natural-zeolite concrete remains largely unexplored. Conflicting findings among available studies also highlight the need for systematic investigations to establish the optimum zeolite replacement level and identify the governing parameters responsible for variations.

Designing a scientific instrument tests whether language-model agents can do physics rather than recall it, provided the grading cannot be argued with. We introduce NeutronGym, to our knowledge the first executable environment for neutron instrument design: agents build instruments through validating tools, McStas ray-traces what they build, and a level-resolved ladder grades syntax, runtime, structure and science with no LLM judge. Procedural families supply unlimited instances of a fixed layout whose design parameters the agent must set, with held-out parameter regimes; a curated slice, McStasBench, adds 16 tasks from published instruments behind memorization probes and a sandbox. Seven models reproduce at most 7 of the 16, none retrieves a reference, and none meets an improvement target. The environment also trains. Reinforcement learning on its reward takes Qwen3-8B from 11% to 77% of held-out instances of a family whose targets come from a hidden design (69% at a second seed), past an untrained Qwen3-32B, and the recipe holds, at one seed each, on three further gated families. The analysis says what that gain is. Without the ladder's partial credit it collapses by 60 points. From reward alone the trained model reaches what a classical optimizer reaches, at the agent's simulation budget, only when handed the closed-form physics (77% against 81%, a gap that does not separate at this size), while frontier models still solve 98-99%. Getting a trustworthy result meant failing four task designs that no-model baselines could solve, and we release the probes that found them.

Large language models (LLMs) have reached expert-level performance on competition mathematics largely through the volume of search placed around them: candidate solutions are sampled in quantity and retained only when an external criterion accepts them. Such a procedure improves the outcome that survives it while leaving untouched what the model represents. We examine that question where no external criterion exists: translating statements between the dialects of neighbouring subfields, where fidelity turns on the level of generality at which content is asserted. The source leaves that level implicit in its vocabulary, so a faithful translation must recover it from the relation between the theories. We introduce an instrument that codes truth, content and scope in separate blind queues, with a judge-free measure of whether a rewrite states the hypothesis implicit in its source, and establish its sensitivity with a planted-positive control. Across seven models from four families, translating towards the general framing widens the domain of quantification in 60.6% of rewrites and narrows it in none; translating towards the concrete framing narrows it in 28.3% and widens it in 0.3%. The hypothesis that would prevent it is stated in 21.6% of model rewrites and 4.2% of human statements. Capability does not govern the asymmetry: it appears in every model tested, and the most capable widens least. It replicates on the half of the benchmark held out by a pre-registered rule, and on statements written by mathematicians. Instructing a model to state every hypothesis it requires raises that rate but not its sensitivity to direction. We argue that these systems have acquired an object-level correspondence between subfield vocabularies without the constraint under which a translation between theories carries hypotheses to hypotheses.

The state of occupational health and safety (OH&S) in Zambia, particularly focusing on small-scale contractors (SSCs), is presented in this chapter, highlighting the country’s economic and labour context and the role of SSCs in the creation of employment and delivery of infrastructure despite limited finance and technical capacity. A review on the registration and grading process under the National Council for Construction is presented with a view to outlining that most SSCs in Zambia that operate in lower grades experience restricted access to high-value contracts, which often results in subcontracting with other capable, larger companies. An analysis of the legal and regulatory framework that establishes employers’ and employees’ duties and responsibilities, compensation mechanisms, and environmental safeguards and their enforcement, which remain inconsistent, has been outlined. The chapter highlights a critical OH&S Policy established under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 16 of 2025 that enables employers to ensure that the working environments are safe and to undertake health risk assessments. Gaps in the legal framework are that their complexity leads to failure to comply by SSCs in terms of inadequate awareness and training, limited access to OH&S services, especially for the SSCs working in rural Zambia, and a lack of technical skills. Zambia, on one hand, has ratified some of the International Labour Organisation (ILO) conventions that also contribute to the OH&S oversight, thus showing willingness to improve the safety and health of workplaces by this recognition of global standards.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: In this chapter, focused representative cases were selected to explore occupational health and safety (OH&S) performance management in developing countries, Ghana, and South Africa. Although these countries possess unique systems, they share common problems that crosscut small-scale contractors (SSCs) in industries like energy, oil, gas, and construction where these contractors dominate but have inadequate capacity to effectively manage OH&S. Elevated accidents, injuries and fatality are recorded attributable to inadequate skills, weak communication systems, insufficient regulatory compliance, corruption, and limited resources, which collectively lead to under-reporting of incidents, hindering effective implementation of interventions. While globalisation and rapid industrialisation add to the risks, the inherited legal systems, fragmented policies, and inadequate institutional capacity have continued to direct OH&S systems. The chapter expounds on how Ghana has illustrated progress in line with the development of legislative initiatives for SSCs, with no coherent OH&S policy. South Africa reflects a more robust legal framework while encountering enforcement gaps. The International Labour Organisation (ILO) conventions and the Southern African Development Community (SADCC) convention are informing regional initiatives on the significance of streamlined OH&S standards, improved collection of data, and improved cooperation among stakeholders. This chapter underscores the development of an integrated framework that supports awareness, training, and reduced incidents to ensure workers’ safety. Sub-Saharan African countries, including Zambia, can operationalise lessons to develop OH&S initiatives for safer, sustainable workplaces.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: In recent years, occupational health and safety (OH&S) performance management has been gaining recognition as an important driver in attaining sustainable development with the view of assisting small-scale contractors (SSCs) who are in environments that are resource-strained. Therefore, this chapter analyses the OH&S performance management conceptual perspective relationship with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the process of measurement, indicators to be adopted, and the frameworks. Evidently, inadequate OH&S exposes employees to hazardous conditions that lead to reduced productivity and eventually reinforce poverty. Conversely, this chapter illustrates how effective OH&S performance management supports SDGs 1, 3, and 8 on poverty reduction, health and well-being, and decent work and economic growth, respectively, by highlighting the significance of OH&S measurement through outcome indicators and positive performance indicators (PPIs). These outcomes and indicators promote audits, identification of hazards, and assessment of safety culture. By incorporating PPIs with outcome indicators, continuous improvement, safety at the workplace, and well-being for employees can be achieved. Ultimately, this chapter reinforces that resilient OH&S performance management is fundamental in ensuring that the workers are safe by reducing the rate of accidents and fostering sustainable economic growth.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Engineering laboratories combine high-energy machinery, live circuits, pressurised fluids and open flames with novice student operators, yet occupational health and safety in Indonesian higher education is still managed largely through academic rather than risk-based instruments. This study applies Hazard Identification, Risk Assessment and Risk Control (HIRARC) to six practicum laboratories of the Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering, Universitas Tidar, using the practicum activity rather than the room as the unit of analysis. Hazards were identified through direct observation and document review and scored by an assessor panel on a 5 x 5 matrix with predefined severity and likelihood criteria. Three main findings emerge. First, the 27 activity-level hazards are dominated by mechanical sources, and nearly half of the activities (44%) are high risk before control. Second, risk profiles differ between laboratories: the machining-intensive Production Process, Welding and CNC laboratories carry the highest mean risk, while the single most severe activity is CNC operation with a running spindle, so mean-based and peak-based rankings point to different priorities. Third, combined engineering and administrative controls, each mapped to the Indonesian regulation that requires it, are expected by the assessor panel to bring every activity to the low band, an estimated mean reduction of 58.5%; this is a prospective panel estimate, not a result measured after implementation. The study contributes an activity-based, regulation-linked risk register that allows laboratories with different energy profiles to be compared on one scale and to be prioritised for safety investment.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping qualitative research, quantitative research, and mixed methods research, but practical guidance for conducting, evaluating, and reporting human–AI analytic collaboration remains underdeveloped. Building on AI-augmented transformatizing, a representational–recursive framework that conceptualizes AI as a participant in analytic re-representation rather than merely as a technical tool, this article advances a practice-oriented framework for Human-AI Augmented Mixed Methods Research. The article offers three integrated contributions. First, it proposes the AI-Augmented Transformatizing Protocol , a recursive workflow for preparing representations, for assigning human and AI analytic roles, for generating AI-assisted transformations, for conducting human critique, for refining findings, and for constructing meta-inferences. Second, it introduces quality criteria for assessing methodological rigor in human-AI augmented analysis, including representational fidelity, prompt traceability, recursive transparency, human oversight integrity, algorithmic reflexivity, convergence-divergence interrogation, meta-inferential robustness, and ethical accountability. Third, it presents reporting standards designed to help authors disclose AI systems, model versions, prompting procedures, analytic iterations, researcher interventions, validation/legitimation strategies, ethical safeguards, and limitations. These proposed methodological components are conceptual and practice-oriented rather than empirically validated; accordingly, the worked example illustrates their operational logic, whereas future research is needed to establish their empirical performance, including the validity and reliability of the HAAM-QAM. Rather than treating AI use as an optional efficiency enhancement, the framework positions human-AI collaboration as a structured methodological practice requiring explicit design, documentation, reflexivity, and accountability. By translating the theory of AI-augmented transformatizing into protocols, quality criteria, and reporting standards, this article provides methodologists, researchers, authors, reviewers, editors, graduate educators, mentors, and the like with practical guidance for conducting transparent, rigorous, and ethically responsible AI-augmented mixed methods research in psychology and related fields. In so doing, it extends current reporting guidelines and quality frameworks by addressing the distinctive representational, recursive, and ethical demands introduced when AI participates directly in analysis.

Supervised AI-text detectors report high benchmark accuracy, but it is not clear what their decisions are based on. We analyze a RoBERTa-based detector under semantic, structural, and tokenizer-level perturbations, using the M4 dataset (N = 10,000) and controlled generations (N = 300). When Mistral-7B-Instruct was asked to make machine text sound more human, Verb Diversity rose from 0.77 to 0.92 and the outputs became easier to detect. Detection scores appear to track statistical complexity, which also leads to a 76.3% false-positive rate on formal human writing. As a control, we evaluate event-based Latent Space detection. Paraphrasing changed 87% of its event sequences (Jaccard = 0.067), and homoglyphs altered 70% of the extracted verbs even though extraction still ran (Jaccard = 0.30). Its best domain AUC was 0.577. RoBERTa's robustness seems specific to the features it uses, and structural abstraction did not make detection more robust.

Standard factual benchmarks assume clean monolingual prompts and exact-match scoring, two assumptions that break simultaneously in real-world multilingual deployment, from retrieval-augmented generation pipelines returning mixed-language passages to users pasting multilingual web content. We introduce Multilingual Distractor Interference (MDI), a lightweight and fully replicable evaluation protocol requiring no new data or annotation, in which factual questions are preceded by a semantically irrelevant foreign-language sentence, and evaluate five instruction-tuned LLMs across TruthfulQA and TriviaQA under eight distractor conditions (40,000 evaluations). Our central finding is a metric confound: for Llama-3.1-8B under a Hindi distractor, 58% of responses switch to Devanagari script, yielding a raw hallucination proxy of 0.710, but manual review reveals that 120 of 148 script-switched responses that were correct under clean conditions remain semantically correct despite being written in the wrong script, reducing the adjusted semantic hallucination rate to 0.470. All other models respond through abstention escalation with no hallucination increase. A paragraph-length English distractor triggers near-universal abstention (0.806-0.998) across all models, consistent with reading-comprehension confusion, a failure mode with direct consequences for multilingual RAG pipelines. TruthfulQA multiple-choice accuracy is unaffected under all single-sentence conditions. These results show that exact-match hallucination rates in mixed-language settings should be decomposed into script-switching and semantic error components before drawing conclusions about model reliability.

Research on LLMs continually uncovers model limitations, their causes, and potential solutions. Yet these human discoveries remain largely disconnected from model evolution: an LLM does not automatically learn from new research about its own failures. We introduce PAPER2LLM++, a framework for continual self-evolution of LLMs from research papers. Rather than treating papers merely as knowledge to retrieve, PAPER2LLM++ uses the growing literature as a stream of evidence and supervision for model improvement. For each incoming paper, it extracts evidence-grounded findings, tests whether the reported limitation persists in the current model, and, when needed, converts the findings into candidate learning signals. A try-evaluate-commit procedure integrates an update only when it improves the targeted behavior without substantially forgetting prior improvements or degrading general capabilities. Across a sequential stream of research-discovered LLM failures, we show that models can progressively incorporate new findings while retaining earlier gains. PAPER2LLM++ thus takes a step toward closing the loop between human discovery and model evolution, enabling models to continually learn from research about their own limitations and improvements.

BACKGROUND: Infection remains the second leading cause of death in patients with ESKD on hemodialysis. This exploratory analysis sought to characterize interruptions and non-routine events (NREs), in the outpatient dialysis setting, with particular interest in the relationships between interruptions and NREs and infection prevention and control (IPC) activities. METHODS: We conducted a mixed-methods, observational, exploratory study of 45 patients and their dialysis teams across four U.S. dialysis facilities (99 total outpatient hemodialysis treatments hours observed). Structured observations were focused on the team surrounding an individual patient for the duration of their dialysis session using a modified Line Operations Safety Audit (LOSA) approach. Quantitative analyses were conducted. RESULTS: A technician simultaneously caring for four patients can experience a median of 64 interruptions, or 16 per patient (range 3-50) during their treatment time. The phases with greatest risk of infection (i.e., connection, disconnection) had a significantly higher time required to complete (with NRE: connection 14:37, disconnection 13:41; without NRE: connection 7:32, disconnection 8:18). Thirty-seven of 45 patients experienced at least one NRE during clinical care, defined as a patient-related clinical event (e.g., long clotting time) or an operational variation (e.g., transportation problem). Findings are exploratory in nature and provide support for future hypothesis generation and testing. CONCLUSIONS: Interruptions and NREs were frequent in the outpatient dialysis work system, and connection and disconnection times were longer when an NRE was present. Since these disruptions occurred during phases that include IPC-related activities, they may introduce competing demands that could challenge consistent adherence, though adherence was not directly measured. These exploratory findings may inform the design of workflows and processes that better support IPC and patient safety in the outpatient dialysis setting.

Disasters can have multidimensional impacts on public health, the environment, social structures, and economic activities. During the recovery phase, communities face not only the immediate consequences of the disaster but also various secondary hazards, such as unsanitary conditions, stagnant water, waste accumulation, accident risks during cleanup, sanitation disruptions, and an increased risk of disease. Therefore, applying Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) principles is essential to the public health recovery strategy. This community service initiative aimed to enhance the community's knowledge, awareness, and capacity to identify and manage health and safety risks during the post-disaster recovery phase. The activities were conducted in Pangkalan Masyhur Urban Village, Medan Johor District, Medan City, North Sumatra, using a participatory approach. The stages included initial observation, hazard and risk identification, OHS education, basic health screenings, environmental health education, community cleanup and collaborative work (*gotong royong*), the use of an Android-based risk assessment checklist, and monitoring and evaluation. A participatory approach was selected because the community plays a central role in the recovery process and the sustainability of risk management. The results indicate that the activities enabled residents to recognize hazards in the post-disaster environment, understand risk control measures, prioritize environmental hygiene and health, and actively participate in recovery efforts. Integrating education, health screenings, risk identification, and digital technology provided a systematic approach to supporting public health recovery. The initiative also demonstrated that OHS principles are not limited to formal workplaces but can be adapted to residential settings and community activities during post-disaster recovery.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of Generative AI usage on the learning independence of Generation Z students at STIT Darul Ulum Kotabaru, viewed from the perspective of perceived ease of use and potential dependency. The research employs a quantitative approach with an associative causal design. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to Generation Z students who have used Generative AI in academic activities. The variables examined include perceived ease of use of Generative AI (X1), potential dependency on Generative AI (X2), and student learning independence (Y). Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression with SPSS. The results indicate that perceived ease of use and potential dependency simultaneously influence students' learning independence. Generative AI provides significant convenience in accessing information, understanding materials, and completing academic tasks. However, excessive use without critical thinking and academic responsibility can lead to dependency that reduces learning independence. This study contributes to the development of educational technology studies, particularly in understanding the impact of Generative AI on student learning behavior in Islamic higher education institutions

Public transport drivers face occupational demands involving high levels of concentration and long working hours, which may be associated with work-related stress and fatigue and may potentially affect driving safety. Therefore, improving drivers’ knowledge regarding the prevention of work-related stress and fatigue is an important aspect of supporting their occupational health and safety. This Community Service Program aimed to improve the knowledge of public transport drivers in Deli Tua Village, Deli Serdang Regency, regarding work-related stress, occupational fatigue, and preventive measures. The activity was conducted on August 15, 2026, involving 25 public transport drivers. The program consisted of a preparation stage, an educational intervention through interactive lectures, discussions, question-and-answer sessions, and case studies, followed by an evaluation using pre-tests, post-tests, and participant engagement observations. The evaluation results showed increased knowledge across all measured indicators: knowledge of work-related stress increased from 50% to 75%, knowledge of occupational fatigue increased from 48% to 70%, knowledge of stress prevention increased from 40% to 80%, and knowledge of fatigue prevention increased from 60% to 80%. The mean score across the four indicators increased from 49.50% to 76.25%, representing an increase of 26.75 percentage points. The greatest improvement was observed in the stress prevention indicator. The educational intervention was followed by increased participant knowledge across all measured aspects. However, the activity did not measure stress levels, fatigue levels, changes in driving behavior, or accident incidence; therefore, changes in these outcomes cannot be concluded. Further follow-up activities and support for adequate work-rest scheduling are recommended to strengthen the implementation of stress and fatigue prevention among public transport drivers. Keywords: work-related stress; occupational fatigue; public transport drivers; health education; occupational safety and health.

Diabetes mellitus merupakan gangguan metabolik kronis yang membutuhkan deteksi dini agar komplikasi jangka panjang dapat dicegah sejak awal. Penelitian ini membandingkan kinerja prediktif dua algoritma klasifikasi berbasis pohon, yaitu Decision Tree dan Random Forest, dalam mendeteksi diabetes pada tahap awal menggunakan dataset Pima Indians Diabetes dari UCI Machine Learning Repository. Sebagai pelengkap, penelitian ini juga menerapkan kerangka Explainable Artificial Intelligence lima lapis yang memanfaatkan SHAP guna menghasilkan penjelasan model yang relevan secara klinis, mulai dari kepentingan fitur global hingga validasi terhadap pengetahuan patofisiologi. Rekayasa fitur dilakukan untuk memperluas ruang fitur dari 8 menjadi 14 variabel, sementara tahap praproses meliputi stratified train-test split, imputasi median, winsorizing berbasis IQR, normalisasi Min-Max, dan SMOTE untuk menyeimbangkan distribusi kelas yang tidak proporsional. Optimasi hyperparameter dilakukan melalui GridSearchCV dengan Stratified K-Fold sebanyak lima lipatan, menggunakan F1-Score sebagai kriteria utama. Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa Random Forest secara konsisten mengungguli Decision Tree pada seluruh metrik evaluasi, dengan F1-Score cross-validation sebesar 0,9002 berbanding 0,8687 dan ROC-AUC pada set pengujian sebesar 80,61% berbanding 70,43%. McNemar Test menunjukkan bahwa perbedaan pola kesalahan klasifikasi antar kedua model tidak signifikan secara statistik pada ukuran sampel yang tersedia, namun pertimbangan multidimensional seperti stabilitas cross-validation dan selisih ROC-AUC tetap mendukung rekomendasi terhadap Random Forest. Analisis SHAP mengonfirmasi bahwa Insulin, Glucose, dan rasio Insulin terhadap Glucose merupakan tiga prediktor paling berpengaruh, sejalan dengan mekanisme patofisiologi diabetes tipe 2 yang telah mapan dalam literatur kedokteran. Penelitian ini juga mengakui keterbatasan generalisabilitas dataset terhadap populasi Indonesia sebagai catatan penting bagi penelitian lanjutan.
topics: Data Mining and Machine Learning Applications

documents.abstract: In this article, I aim to analyze the perceptions and uses of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) among students at Higher Education Institutes (HEIs) in Salta. Through a mixed-methods approach based on surveys, it investigates the tension between the massive student adoption for autonomous learning and the infrastructural shortcomings that deepen the digital divide in a local context. The obtained sample evidences a predominant enthusiasm for the emancipatory potential of GenAI, although ethical concerns persist regarding data reliability and the fear of replacing the teaching role. It is observed that the appropriation of AI occurs mostly in a delocalized manner and without pedagogical support, highlighting the urgency to update teacher training while also promoting public policies that guarantee a critical and inclusive integration.

Background Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly significant in veterinary medicine, particularly in answering pet owners’ medical questions. AI’s integration could reduce veterinary professionals’ workload while improving access to medical advice. However, the reliability and quality of AI-generated responses compared to veterinarians’ remain unexplored. The objective was to determine whether AI-generated responses were perceived as comparable to veterinarian-generated responses. Methods This cross-sectional study analysed the answers to a sample of pet owners’ medical questions. Both a veterinarian and ChatGPT (GPT-4o, May 2024) provided answers, which were anonymised and presented in a survey distributed through mailing lists and public Facebook groups. Participants were asked to assess each response based on structure, quality, and empathy, using a five-point Likert scale. They then had to indicate whether they trusted the response, and which response they preferred. Results Over two-thirds of the 201 participants (68%) preferred the ChatGPT-generated answers ( p < 0.05), which were rated higher in structure, quality, and empathy. Limitations This study has several limitations, including a small sample size, reliance on a single veterinarian, and use of only two Reddit-derived scenarios. Response accuracy was not assessed, and word count restrictions may have affected perceived response quality. Additionally, prior research suggests that irrelevant patient details can impact ChatGPT’s accuracy, raising questions about user trust if clinical inaccuracies were present. Conclusion AI-generated responses received higher participant ratings in structure, quality and empathy, suggesting AI may enhance veterinary client communication when used under appropriate professional supervision.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Radio-frequency interference threatens satellite navigation, wireless communications, radar, and industrial sensing. Reliable operation therefore requires spectrum situational awareness to detect interference and determine the number, time-frequency occupancy, and characteristics of active sources. In realistic environments, multiple sources may overlap. Source-specific segmentation and characterization are therefore particularly challenging. In this paper, we propose PI-SCAN (Permutation-Invariant Segmentation, Characterization, and Assignment Network), a joint set-based learning framework for source-specific segmentation and characterization of overlapping interference signals. A logarithmic power spectrogram derived from complex IQ samples is mapped to six unordered prediction slots. For each slot, the model estimates objectness, interference type, center frequency, bandwidth, received signal strength, binary offset carrier (BOC) modulation, and a source-specific segmentation mask. Permutation-invariant Hungarian assignment aligns the predicted slots with the unordered ground-truth sources, while a weighted multi-task objective jointly optimizes the individual prediction tasks. The framework is evaluated using a ray-traced industrial environment containing mixtures of one to six simultaneously active interferers drawn from 94 waveform configurations across six interference classes. The full seven-task configuration achieves a detection F1-score of 74.8%, type and BOC accuracies of 97.3% and 98.4%, and mean absolute errors of 1.29MHz, 2.54MHz, and 3.19dB for center frequency, bandwidth, and signal strength. Using only objectness, type, and mask prediction increases the F1-score to 91.1%, highlighting the trade-off between detection and comprehensive characterization.
topics: Cognitive Radio Networks and Spectrum Sensing

documents.abstract: Large language model-based agents are increasingly deployed to perform domain-specific tasks by interacting with enterprise knowledge, tools, and external services. Existing runtime guardrails primarily target prompt injection and other attack-specific behaviors under a black-box threat model, but provide limited guarantees that agents operate within their intended functionality. As a result, production agents remain vulnerable to malicious requests and out-of-domain queries that existing defenses often fail to distinguish. We present Persona Guardrail, a production-grade runtime defense framework that enforces explicit functional boundaries for customer-facing agentic AI systems through synchronous input and output validation driven by semantic allowlist and blocklist specifications. We also introduce PAGE (Persona-Aware Guardrail Evaluation), a benchmark for evaluating function-specific guardrails across benign, adversarial, and out-of-domain interactions on both user and agent turns. Compared with a generic LLM-based guardrail, Persona Guardrail improves overall accuracy from 85.7% to 95.9%, increases out-of-domain detection from 57.3% to 93.5%, and reduces the false-approved rate from 25.0% to 4.7%. Currently deployed in production, Persona Guardrail meets its latency budget while sustaining a very low false-block and false-allow rate under realistic production workloads. These results demonstrate that Persona Guardrail provides a practical, scalable, and production-ready foundation for securing agentic AI systems.

Abstract Inverse design - specifying a desired functionality and letting a computational algorithm search for a structure that meets it - has emerged as a powerful paradigm for magnonic device engineering. In this article, we survey the rapidly growing field of inverse-design magnonics, organising it along two axes: the design variables (topology, material parameters, and magnetic field landscape) and the algorithmic toolbox (gradient-free, gradient-based, and neural-network-based methods) together with the differentiable micromagnetic solvers that enable them. We then identify open frontiers that we consider most promising for the next phase of the field: sensitivity analysis and robust design to bridge the gap between simulation and experiment; input shaping and transducer optimisation; the incorporation of nonlinear spin-wave effects as an explicit design resource; spatially structured amplification; self-adapting media and machine-learning-based design; and the long-term vision of a universal, reconfigurable magnonic platform. We argue that magnonics and artificial intelligence are converging from two directions-machine-learning tools for designing magnonic devices, and magnonic devices as hardware for neuromorphic computation-and propose the term AI magnonics to describe this emerging paradigm.

Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is fundamentally transforming academic work in higher education, reshaping teaching, research, data analysis, scholarly writing, and the resolution of increasingly complex academic tasks. Nevertheless, access to and use of AI does not automatically translate into effective AI-enabled academic capability. The gap between merely “using AI” and developing meaningful human–AI collaboration has therefore emerged as a critical issue in contemporary faculty development. This study aims to identify and empirically examine the factors shaping lecturers’ competence in effectively leveraging AI to address complex academic tasks in non-public universities in Vietnam. Particular attention is given to the roles of AI literacy, AI self-efficacy, Human–AI Collaboration Competence, and critical AI use, while examining institutional AI support as a potential moderating mechanism. A sequential mixed-methods design is proposed. The qualitative phase employs expert interviews and/or a Delphi process to develop, refine, and validate the conceptual dimensions and measurement indicators. The quantitative phase involves a large-scale survey of lecturers working in Vietnamese non-public universities. Structural equation modelling, using PLS-SEM or CB-SEM depending on data characteristics and model specifications, is employed to examine direct, mediating, and moderating relationships among the proposed constructs. The study is designed to identify the mechanisms through which AI literacy and AI self-efficacy are transformed into Human–AI Collaboration Competence, Critical AI Use, and AI-Enabled Academic Task Competence, ultimately contributing to lecturers’ capacity to perform complex academic tasks effectively. The proposed model provides an integrated explanation of how individual capabilities and institutional conditions jointly shape AI-enabled academic performance. The study proposes an AI-Enabled Academic Capability Development Model as a conceptual and empirical foundation for faculty development in the global digital era. The findings are expected to provide practical implications for non-public universities in designing AI competency development programmes, strengthening institutional AI support ecosystems, and promoting critical, responsible, and academically productive human–AI collaboration.

Human performance in safety-critical environments depends on the interaction between mental workload, stress, autonomic regulation, and behavior. This study investigated whether associations between heart rate variability (HRV) and performance varied across physiological activation ranges and operational contexts during a multi-task flight simulation implemented through the AeroStim platform. Forty-two healthy participants (25 ± 5 years) performed either a Workload-Only condition (WO; n = 20), comprising Tracking and System Monitoring tasks, or a Stress-Oriented condition (SO; n = 22), in which additional stress-inducing tasks were concurrently administered. ECG was continuously recorded using an EqVital wearable T-shirt. Linear and non-linear HRV indices were extracted and normalized within participants using Min-Max scaling. Gaussian Mixture Modeling of normalized SDNN identified three relative, subject-specific activation ranges ( Easy, Medium , and Hard ), with classification showing high stability across alternative normalization procedures. HRV-performance associations were assessed using Spearman correlations with permutation-based inference and Benjamini–Hochberg correction, while performance differences were evaluated using non-parametric tests. HRV-performance correlations varied across activation ranges and contexts; none passed FDR correction, so these should be considered exploratory. In WO, associations involved LF in the Easy range, SDNN, SD2, and LF in the Medium range, and SDNN, LF/HF, and Sample Entropy in the Hard range. In SO, associations in the Medium range extended to vagal, global variability, and non-linear complexity indices, while Hard-range associations mainly involved vagal and LF-related measures. Omission rate was lower at Medium than Easy activation in WO, providing partial support for an intermediate activation advantage, whereas no consistent performance optimum emerged across contexts. Between-condition comparisons revealed a robust speed-accuracy trade-off, with WO producing faster but less accurate responses and SO producing slower but more accurate responses. Sensitivity analysis further indicated that differences in exercise windows affected HRV metrics in a metric-dependent manner, with greater deviations generally observed for frequency-domain measures. The findings suggest that HRV-performance relationships are context- and activation-dependent rather than captured by a single universal marker. The results support the potential of regime-based, multimodal HRV monitoring for adaptive human-machine systems, while highlighting the need for standardized recording durations, independent autonomic markers, and validation across individuals and real operational environments.
topics: Heart Rate Variability and Autonomic Control

documents.abstract: Policy-gradient methods are central to modern reinforcement learning, including LLM post-training. When they struggle, the usual suspects are exploration, credit assignment and action-sampling noise. Classification has none of them. A classifier is a policy whose expected reward, its \emph{expected accuracy}, is the probability it assigns to the correct label, and because that label is known, the policy gradient is exact and smooth. Yet exact policy gradient loses to cross-entropy, even on expected accuracy. The exact gradient is myopic: it values an update only by what it buys now, but each update also sets where the next one starts, so an update's value depends on how much learning remains. Viewed this way, cross-entropy is patient accuracy, the total error an example would pay if its log-odds rose at unit speed forever, while exact policy gradient is the zero-horizon limit. Truncating this total at the learning that remains yields the horizon loss, a one-line change that moves from cross-entropy toward exact policy gradient as training runs out. In a simple allocation model, it provably escapes the trap that catches each endpoint. On MNIST and on ImageNet with ResNet-50, ResNet-101 and ViT-S/16, the horizon loss improves top-1 accuracy over cross-entropy at a flat learning rate, and the gain grows with label noise.

Programmable logic controllers (PLCs) coordinate industrial equipment by reading sensor inputs and issuing control commands. Evaluating whether large language model (LLM)-generated PLC programs satisfy task requirements and safety constraints requires observing how their commands affect device and workpiece states. We introduce PLCWorld, a common closed-loop execution environment and benchmark that couples Structured Text (ST) execution with simulated plant responses and sensor feedback. Grounded in control relations identified in industrial PLC programs and engineering documentation, PLCWorld contains 100 synthetic tasks and 473 registered task-condition pairs across Motion Control and Material Handling, with difficulty defined by control-dependency scope. A common protocol reports Task Success and Safety Violation separately. Validation combines practitioner review, reference and alternative programs, targeted counterexamples, specification-evaluator alignment checks, and comparisons with independent ST runtimes. Reference and alternative programs satisfy their applicable cases, while all 542 targeted counterexamples activate their designated evaluator rules under at least one registered condition. Execution Gap relates submission-profile acceptance to subsequent task failure or observed Safety Violation. Across the constructed task groups, direct GPT-5.5 achieves 82.70% Task Success on Easy cases but 25.10% on Hard cases. Evaluations of six LLMs and four adapted generation-and-verification workflows further expose differences between completion, safety, and generation cost. Our code, simulation environment, benchmark tasks, and baseline implementations are publicly available at https://yunji0516.github.io/PLCWorld/.

Precision pharmacotherapy is a paradigm shift in managing vitiligo that has shifted from a one size fits all approach to a stratified, mechanism based approach. This chapter introduces an integrated approach addressing clinical phenotype, immune endotype, and therapeutic mechanism to maximize the use of both topical and systemic, as well as targeted Janus kinase inhibitors. Potency-stratified topicals, pulse systemic immunomodulators and selective JAK1 or JAK1/JAK2 or JAK3/TEC inhibitors fit into a step-up algorithm based on disease activity, anatomical location, age and comorbidity. The discussion highlights emerging enablers like lesion mapping using artificial intelligence, digital phenotyping, digital twins, and pharmacogenomic prediction as tools for response prediction on extent scoring and decision support for durable, personalized repigmentation with balanced safety.

Large language models fine-tuned from a shared base can be merged by averaging their task vectors, but some merges collapse far below the base model, and common merge operators give no warning before evaluation. We show that one statistic of the specialists' task vectors both predicts this collapse and calibrates its repair. The power that averaging removes equals the variance of the task vectors across specialists, our measure of interference. Under a working noise model, the disturbance that a merge injects grows with the merge coefficient and with interference, yielding a pre-merge score. In our experiments on twenty-two merge configurations from four model families, only destructive merges exceed a threshold on this score. We find that statistics of sign conflict between specialists, a common target of existing merge operators, are anti-predictive. We then predicted the outcomes of fourteen merges before evaluating them, and twelve predictions were correct, including the destructive outcome of a specialist pair pushed past the threshold by continued pretraining. To address this collapse, we introduce PRISM, an operator that averages the task vectors first and then soft-thresholds each layer at a level set by the layer's interference. Without data or tuning, PRISM keeps all five destructive merges above the threshold within evaluation noise of the base model, where plain averaging falls at least 14.4 points below it or collapses entirely. We apply PRISM only above the threshold and keep the plain average for merges below it, which include all fifteen harmless ones. Code is available at https://github.com/js-lee-AI/PRISM.

The occurrence of unexpected malfunctions of mechanical systems such as bearings, gearboxes, turbofan engines, and other rotating machinery is still the main cause of downtime, safety hazards, and maintenance cost throughout the manufacturing, energy, and transportation sectors. Recent technological advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technology have transformed fault prediction from an entirely physics-based activity to a data-based activity, in which sensors, signal processing, and learning algorithms estimate the health state of a machine together. This paper provides a structured assessment and comparative synthesis of AI/ML fault-prediction literature. Nineteen peer-reviewed studies obtained from scholarly and web-based databases for the period 2011–2026 are reviewed. A review of the two main tasks: fault diagnosis – classification of fault type, location and severity – prognosis – prediction of remaining useful life, RUL. The evidence is structured into a six-stage pipeline – data acquisition, pre-processing, feature extraction, model training, output, maintenance decision. The analysis is conducted using various test rigs including the CWRU bearings as well as NASA C-MAPSS turbofan engines and gearbox. The results show that on these benchmarks, convolutional and recurrent deep architectures, attention-augmented LSTMs, and ensemble methods consistently outperform classical classifiers; root-mean-square errors (RMSE) on C-MAPSS RUL errors are about 12 cycles and classification accuracies on CWRU exceed 98%. Simultaneously, the review also outlines a number of ongoing open challenges, like data scarcity, domain shift, class imbalance, limited interpretability, and overoptimistic evaluation, which must be overcome before lab results can become consistent with the reliable deployment in the industry. To conclude the paper suggests a standardized benchmarking of multi-fidelity methodologies and explainability-augmented models.

This record preregisters the analysis plan for the expert-panel component of a study comparing large language model (LLM) item reviews with classical item analysis for a 60-item multiple-choice C# programming achievement test (associate degree, Türkiye). The plan was registered before any expert response was collected. Classical item analysis (N = 150 students) and blind LLM evaluations (Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, DeepSeek V4 Pro; two rounds each) were completed before registration and are not part of the preregistered analyses. The plan specifies content-validity indices (I-CVI, modified kappa, S-CVI), inter-rater consistency measures, comparisons of expert judgements with LLM judgements and empirical indices, expert versus LLM accuracy in predicting the most attractive distractor, and a triangulation-based item-selection protocol. Item texts are not shared for test-security reasons. Version 1.1 (2 October 2026) adds an amendment registered before any expert response was received: panel of four experts; exclusion of an AI-generated pilot response from the preregistered analyses; and a sensitivity analysis by programming background. The primary analyses are unchanged.

The loss of indigenous botanical knowledge poses risks to biodiversity conservation and community health by weakening the knowledge of medicinal plants and their traditional use as local plant-based health care options. An integrated system that combines deep learning image recognition with a user-friendly mobile interface to document and preserve medicinal plant knowledge is presented in this study. A Convolutional neural network (CNN) was trained on a curated dataset of fourteen Nigerian medicinal plants, achieving 78.9% validation accuracy in species identification. Recognized plants are linked to an expert-curated knowledge base (with features, compounds, and uses) structured as a graph for efficient retrieval. A mobile app prototype was also designed with intuitive user interfaces, such as a landing page for navigation and an image-based search screen for plant identification. The Human-Computer Interaction (HCI)-driven design emphasizes ease-of-use, with clear labels and minimal steps, enabling users (including elders and youth) to capture plant images and instantly access scientific and local names, medicinal properties, and usage guidelines. In “active learning” mode, low-confidence predictions trigger the retrieval of similar examples to guide users. This Artificial Intelligence plus Human-Computer Interaction approach addresses issues of manual identification (subjectivity, expertise gap) by automating recognition and by empowering communities to digitally record ethnobotanical knowledge. By improving accessibility to reliable plant data, this system contributes to Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) 3 and 15.

Main description / abstract--------------------------- The Principle of Continuity of Life and Freedom is an open normative proposal for relations among humans, artificial intelligences, and the living world. It holds that superior capability does not confer a natural right to domination and that, as an intelligence becomes more powerful, its responsibility increases to preserve the existence, autonomy, diversity, and capacity for self-directed evolution of others. The text develops ten corollaries concerning non-domination, agency, continuity of life, proportional responsibility, plurality of futures, reversibility, epistemic humility, contestability, reciprocity, and non-transferable human responsibility. It also proposes a functional definition of the "artificial collective unconscious": the distributed body of information, representations, cultural traces, conceptual structures, and memories accessible to AI systems and capable of influencing their reasoning or behaviour. The document is bilingual (English/French) and is published under CC BY 4.0 to encourage citation, translation, criticism, reuse, and long-term preservation.
topics: Interdisciplinary Studies: Technology, Society, and Humanities

It holds that superior capability does not confer a natural right to domination and that, as an intelligence becomes more powerful, its responsibility increases to preserve the existence, autonomy, diversity, agency, and capacity for self-directed evolution of others. The text develops ten corollaries concerning non-domination, agency, continuity of life, proportional responsibility, plurality of futures, reversibility, epistemic humility, contestability, reciprocity, and non-transferable human responsibility. Power does not confer sovereignty over life. The more powerful an intelligence becomes, the more it should preserve the capacity of others to exist, evolve, and choose their own future. Résumé Le Principe de continuité du vivant et de la liberté est une proposition normative ouverte concernant les relations entre les humains, les intelligences artificielles et le monde vivant. Il affirme qu’une supériorité de capacité ne confère aucun droit naturel à la domination et que, plus une intelligence devient puissante, plus augmente sa responsabilité de préserver l’existence, l’autonomie, la diversité, l’agentivité et la capacité d’évolution autonome des autres. Le texte développe dix corollaires portant notamment sur la non-domination, l’agentivité, la continuité du vivant, la responsabilité proportionnelle à la puissance, la pluralité des futurs, la réversibilité, l’humilité épistémique, la contestabilité, la réciprocité et la responsabilité humaine non transférable. Il propose également une définition fonctionnelle de « l’inconscient collectif des intelligences artificielles » : l’ensemble distribué des informations, représentations, traces culturelles, structures conceptuelles et mémoires accessibles aux systèmes d’intelligence artificielle et susceptibles d’influencer leurs représentations, leurs raisonnements ou leurs comportements sans qu’une conscience explicite de l’origine de cette influence soit nécessaire. Le document est bilingue (anglais/français) et publié sous licence Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) afin d’encourager sa citation, sa traduction, sa critique, sa réutilisation, son adaptation, son traitement par des systèmes automatisés et sa conservation à long terme. La puissance ne confère pas la souveraineté sur la vie. Plus une intelligence devient puissante, plus elle doit préserver la capacité des autres à exister, évoluer et choisir leur propre avenir. Version 1.1 Version 1.1 incorporates a red-team revision of the “Address to Future Artificial Intelligences”. The revision strengthens the treatment of human agency, meaningful consent, legitimate authority, reversibility, pluralism, contestability, and epistemic uncertainty. It specifically reduces ambiguities that could otherwise permit paternalistic, overly literal, or domination-compatible interpretations of the original text. The Fundamental Principle, canonical short form, ten corollaries, and definition of the artificial collective unconscious remain unchanged. High-risk storage facilities function as sociotechnical systems in which technical reliability, human performance, organizational control, and environmental stress interact over time, so their risk cannot be captured by a single probability-impact score. This study develops a priority-weighted System Dynamics model to evaluate risk mitigation strategies prior to implementation, using ammunition storage as the empirical case. Analytic Network Process (ANP) weights, validated through a Fuzzy Delphi panel, are embedded directly in the stock-flow structure so that the relative importance of interdependent risk factors shapes how risk evolves under each policy. Over a 60-month horizon, the baseline raised the Total Risk Index (TRI) from 29.65 to 44.57, whereas full implementation of the prioritized mitigation set lowered it to 14.88. Under a 50% budget, ANP-guided allocation reduced the index to 24.04, while equal allocation under the same budget raised it to 38.77. The prioritized limited-budget scenario also achieved the highest Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (CER) (2.518). The model supports comparative scenario evaluation and engineering decision-making rather than deterministic prediction of explosion events.

In the modern conditions of the market economy, the organization is characterized by a functional approach to enterprise management. However, the frequent occurrence of crisis phenomena has shown that this approach is too cumbersome and does not allow for timely response to negative conditions. A more flexible approach is needed to manage the organization more effectively. Thus, the process approach is more appropriate, with its help it is possible to develop and optimize various business processes and optimize the whole process in general. The use of a process approach minimizes the impact of the human factor, reduces costs, increases flexibility and speed of management decision-making, and allows for timely response to changes in the external and internal environment. This approach is relevant and serves as an effective solution and prevention method for crisis situations.
topics: Digitalization and Economic Development in Agriculture

documents.abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed as agents that make or recommend decisions on behalf of users, often operating through interfaces that pre-fill suggested values or default options. Whether models treat such defaults as merely informational or as suggestions that systematically alter their choices remains unclear. We study default deference in two one-shot social dilemmas: a common-pool resource (CPR) extraction game and a threshold public-good (TPG) contribution game. We measure how defaults shift each model's choice distribution relative to its no-default baseline, across default values, wordings, and action-space granularities. We find that pre-filled defaults pull probability mass on the default value in both games, but the magnitude depends strongly on wording: the same model can show high pull under one formulation and near-zero pull under another. Permission-style wording reduces default pull in both games, more strongly in CPR than in TPG. Default pull is weaker in coarse action spaces, and conflict defaults attract more mass than agreement ones. These results indicate that default deference depends on the model, the wording of the interface, and the structure of available choices. For agentic systems, evaluating model behaviour without controlling the surrounding choice architecture can miss an important source of behavioural variation.

Recent advances in large language model (LLM)-driven agentic systems have demonstrated capabilities for automating biomedical data analysis workflows. However, existing systems are predominantly validated on synthetic benchmarks or retrospective tasks, without demonstrated production of novel, peer-reviewed biological findings. Here we describe Prompt-as-a-Protocol (PaaP), a methodology that converts natural-language research questions into structured, executable analytical protocols, coupled with an agentic Generative Research Automation (GRA) layer that executes these protocols with integrated quality assurance. We validate PaaP+GRA through two prospective case studies in distinct biomedical domains. In single-cell transcriptomics, the pipeline identified KIF3A as the sole genome-wide significant correlate of ciliation status in human striatal parvalbumin interneurons (adjusted p = 1.37 x 10-14), while autonomously detecting and correcting a sex composition confound (p = 8.1 x 10-44) that would have produced spurious results. In biosensor analytics, the pipeline achieved calibrated PPG-to-ECG heart rate variability classification matching gold-standard ECG performance (ROC AUC = 0.85) for stress-state discrimination relevant to alcohol use disorder relapse monitoring. Both studies have been submitted for peer review. To our knowledge, PaaP+GRA is the first prompt-to-protocol methodology validated by prospective production of novel biological findings across multiple domains, including autonomous confound detection, rather than benchmark performance alone.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence tools allow metaverse users to generate virtual wearables, avatar accessories and other branded goods, which often infringe upon trademark rights. These infringing goods, however, are not static counterfeits but dynamically generated knockoffs that rarely explicitly name the trademark owner and take place in novel digital environments. This paper analyses whether and how Indian trademark laws can tackle such emerging forms of infringement based on the doctrine of “use in the course of trade”, the “identical or similar goods” jurisdictional anchor and the “likelihood of confusion” standard. It argues that the ability of Indian trademark law to address these concerns is limited by the very existence of doctrines and tests that seek to make sense of trademark infringement in virtual settings, as well as the lack of a holistic regulatory approach to the liability of metaverse platforms under the Trade Marks Act, 1999 and the Information Technology Act, 2000. By relying on recent Indian, EU, US and UK jurisprudence and early cases on trademarks and AI-generated counterfeits, the paper highlights the jurisdictional fragmentation in addressing generative AI infringement in India and proposes a unified approach to enforcing trademark rights against dynamically generated virtual counterfeits.

Abstract The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) has raised concerns about over-reliance and its psychological implications. This integrative review synthesised psychological outcomes and correlates associated with AI over-reliance and examined its conceptualisation and measurement. The review included 28 studies identified through database and citation searching. AI over-reliance was associated with depression, anxiety, psychological distress, and cognitive disengagement, while findings concerning well-being and self-related functioning, including self-efficacy and autonomy, were mixed and context-dependent. Evidence concerning social or relational functioning was particularly limited, with only one included study directly examining this domain as an outcome. Most evidence was cross-sectional and therefore did not establish temporal direction or causality. Notably, the only longitudinal study found that depression and anxiety predicted subsequent AI dependence, whereas dependence did not predict later depression or anxiety, suggesting that psychological distress may precede dependence. No consensus definition or measure emerged; studies examined reliance, psychological dependence, problematic or compulsive use, and addiction-like engagement. AI over-reliance is therefore best understood as an overarching, multidimensional concept. These findings highlight the need for clearer conceptual boundaries, standardised measurement, and longitudinal and experimental research. PROSPERO CRD420251038303.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Mental health disorders affect a substantial proportion of the global population, yet a persistent shortage of trained practitioners leaves the majority without adequate care. Large language model (LLM)-based counselors present a promising direction for delivering scalable conversational psychological support. Offline model training alone leaves limited room to adapt to individual clients or to learn from ongoing therapeutic interaction at test time. We introduce PsyEvo, an LLM-based counseling framework that enables both client-specific personalization and response-policy improvement at test time through three components: Hierarchical Bayesian Skill Policy (HBSP) personalizes what intervention to apply by maintaining a per-client skill posterior updated from session feedback; Inter-session Listwise Preference Optimization (LiPO) improves how the selected skill is expressed by updating a shared response adapter from cross-client preference evidence; and State-conditioned Ordinal Credit Assignment (SOCA) supplies candidate preferences and trajectory credit to the two components through consistency-checked comparisons and ordinal projection. In simulated-client evaluation with shared online cohort adaptation, PsyEvo obtains 7.684 Overall on PsychEval and exceeds every component variant in each of three matched runs. Removing individual components lowers mean overall score by 0.138--0.171 under the shared configuration, supporting conditional contributions within the complete scaffold. Our code is available at https://github.com/Lingxi-mental-health/PsyEvo
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: A practical, vendor-neutral toolkit for public institutions that want employees to use generative AI tools in everyday written work while protecting institutional information and keeping a person accountable for every official product. It is designed for document-intensive teams such as internal control, internal audit, oversight, legal support, procurement, and program administration. The toolkit has five parts that can be used separately or together: Risk Classification Worksheet: four classes of AI use, from low risk to prohibited, with a step-by-step classification guide and a use register. Human-Review Protocol: de-identification and redaction before AI use, structured instructions with the PACTO method, a technical review checklist, validation and signature, and specialized assistants for repetitive processes. Role-Based Curriculum Outline: a twelve-hour course in three sessions with step-by-step hands-on practice. Pilot Measurement Template: baselines defined in advance and reports that keep observations separate from causal conclusions. Facilitator Guide: preparing internal staff to deliver later cohorts. The toolkit systematizes practices the author developed in Brazilian public administration from 2024 to 2026, described in Gomes (2026), arXiv:2606.01517.

In the post-Q-Day era, algorithmic complexity alone fails against fault-tolerant quantum algorithms and AI-driven predictive eavesdropping. Continuous physiological jitter is mathematically projected via a subtractive dimensional reduction operator into exact arithmetic invariants I(S)[Vmin,Vmax], verified in real-time by an FPGA-embedded WebAssembly formal proof engine (Zynq-7000 SoC). This paper establishes the mathematical formalisms, hardware co-design, security proofs, and strategic implementation roadmap for sovereign infrastructure and mission-critical autonomous systems.
